statement: Positive mosquito pools and vector detections do not establish human infection, clinical disease, or local transmission.
notes: Vector detection != pathogen-positive vector != human infection.

statement: Lyme case residence geography does not identify the place of exposure or local transmission.
Building-water or aerosol pathway context does not establish contamination, treatment failure, exposure, infection, or illness.
Source-water contamination, microbial indicators, HABs, nutrient loading, or infrastructure age do not independently establish illness.
NORS and waterborne outbreak reports are investigation-dependent and non-reporting is not pathogen absence.
notes: Outbreak surveillance is not a continuous incidence series.

statement: Laboratory-based Salmonella, Campylobacter, and STEC reporting does not capture all community infections or all exposures.
notes: Detection depends on care-seeking, testing, laboratory methods, and reporting.

statement: FoodNet coverage and participation do not support Western Basin county or neighborhood estimates.
Influenza laboratory positivity, outpatient visits, hospitalizations, and mortality have different denominators and are not one transmission rate.
notes: Testing intensity != disease intensity; hospitalization != community incidence.

statement: Wastewater data provide community-level signals but cannot currently determine the number of infections.
notes: Sewershed coverage and shedding variation remain important limits.

statement: Animal rabies cases, potential exposures, PEP, human infection, and human disease are distinct records.
notes: Animal-human interface does not imply human disease.

statement: NHSN facility participation and HAI measures do not represent community incidence or permit a facility ranking in this baseline.
National antimicrobial-resistance estimates are not transferred to the Western Basin.
Population, settlement, workplace, and mobility context identify system interfaces only; they do not establish contact, exposure, infection, or disease.
Surveillance intensity, testing availability, reporting infrastructure, and laboratory participation are not incidence.
HAB toxic/environmental pathways are not folded into an infectious-disease system or composite score.
Phase 12A/B/C accepted artifacts are reused by reference and remain immutable during Phase 13A.
notes: No vector ecology rebuild or modification.

statement: Accepted climate observations provide environmental context but do not establish causal disease incidence or future behavior.
notes: Historical climate behavior != future disease baseline.

statement: Institutional monitoring, advice, funding, and information are not automatically operational control or legal authority.
